input.query: three dependencies with yield that depend on each other

content.text:
## Answer

The documentation example showing three chained dependencies that each use `yield` and depend on each other is found in the **"Sub-dependencies with `yield`"** section of the FastAPI docs:

- **Doc page**: `docs/en/docs/tutorial/dependencies/dependencies-with-yield.md` (section `## Sub-dependencies with yield`, around lines 62–90)
- **Code example file**: `docs_src/dependencies/tutorial008_an_py310.py`

The doc text explains:
> "For example, `dependency_c` can have a dependency on `dependency_b`, and `dependency_b` on `dependency_a`... In this case `dependency_c`, to execute its exit code, needs the value from `dependency_b` (here named `dep_b`) to still be available. And, in turn, `dependency_b` needs the value from `dependency_a` (here named `dep_a`) to be available for its exit code."

It embeds the actual code from `docs_src/dependencies/tutorial008_an_py310.py` (highlighting lines 6, 14, 22 for the three `yield`-based functions `dependency_a`, `dependency_b`, and `dependency_c`, and lines 18-19, 26-27 for how each function uses the previous one's yielded value in its exit/cleanup code).

This same example is also translated into other language versions of the docs, e.g.:
- `docs/ja/docs/tutorial/dependencies/dependencies-with-yield.md`
- `docs/hi/docs/tutorial/dependencies/dependencies-with-yield.md`
- `docs/zh/docs/tutorial/dependencies/dependencies-with-yield.md`

but they all reference the same underlying source file `docs_src/dependencies/tutorial008_an_py310.py`.
